summary: Recording compression: shrink NVR footage without compromising performance, via four levers. (1) At-rest storage codec (Settings -> Recording): segments can be re-encoded once to H.265/H.264 on the GPU (NVENC) at remux time -- live capture and event clips stay stream-copy, and a shared NVENC concurrency semaphore queues encodes so recording is never blocked. Each segment records its on-disk codec in a new recording_segments.codec column. (2) Playback transcode: HEVC segments are streamed as-is to browsers that can decode them; browsers that can't (Firefox, older browsers) get an on-the-fly HEVC->H.264 transcode on the serve path, so playback works everywhere with no plaintext copy stored. (3) Camera-side H.265 via ONVIF: a per-camera 'Camera-side quality (ONVIF)' control pushes the codec + bitrate cap to the camera's own encoder (Media2/ver20 with Media1 fallback), the zero-host-cost lever -- the change is verified by re-reading from the camera and the actual reason is surfaced if the camera rejects it. (4) Capacity estimator now accounts for the added GPU encode load when host-side re-encoding is on. Defaults are unchanged (storage codec = copy), so existing installs record exactly as before until opted in.
compatibility: Backward compatible. Default storage codec is 'copy' (camera's native codec, no host re-encode), so nothing changes until an operator opts in. The new recording_segments.codec column is additive (legacy rows have an empty codec and play back unchanged). Host-side re-encode and playback transcode require an NVIDIA GPU (NVENC); the capacity estimator flags re-encode enabled without a GPU. Camera-side ONVIF codec changes are best-effort and depend on the camera supporting encoder changes over ONVIF Media2; the storage-codec lever is the camera-agnostic fallback.
